outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the homological Arnold conjecture for Hamiltonian fixed points was already settled over every coefficient field, and over the integers since 2022, so nothing in the window changes that. Inside the window, a 27 August 2026 preprint by Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu claims the transverse Arnold–Givental bound over F₂ but only for Lagrangians that are fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions; a 2 October 2026 preprint by Gong gives a counterexample to a degenerate homological Lagrangian bound and discloses that large language model tools assisted the article; a 2024 preprint and a 2025 preprint give partial degenerate results; a 2026 preprint by Jiao gives partial degenerate results. The degenerate forms and the strong (Morse-critical) forms remain open in general, and the 2026 transverse claim is not yet refereed.
problem_asks: The statement is terse ('Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture – relating symplectic geometry to Morse theory'), so the standard forms it names are spelled out here. (1) Arnold conjecture, nondegenerate / strong form: for a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ of a closed symplectic manifold (M, ω), the number of fixed points is at least the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on M. (2) Arnold conjecture, homological (weak) form: the number of fixed points of a nondegenerate φ is at least the sum of Betti numbers of M, over a field or over ℤ. (3) Arnold conjecture, degenerate form: for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms the number of contractible fixed points is at least cuplength(M)+1. (4) Arnold–Givental conjecture, transverse homological form: for a closed Lagrangian L in a closed symplectic manifold and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ with φ(L) transverse to L, #(L ∩ φ(L)) is at least the sum of Betti numbers of L. (5) Arnold–Givental, strong form: the same count is at least the minimal number of Morse critical points of L; the source I read for the Arnold–Givental statement gives only the homological form, so the strong Lagrangian form is the analogue Arnold stated and I have not verified its wording in a source. (6) Degenerate Arnold–Givental: the Lagrangian bound of (4) without the transversality hypothesis, in homological or cup-length form. Items (1)–(3) concern Hamiltonian fixed points; items (4)–(6) concern Lagrangian intersections. The Morse-theoretic content is the lower bound in each item.

events.what_happened: Floer, 'Morse theory for Lagrangian intersections', J. Differential Geom. 28 (1988) 513–547, as cited by later sources. A 1988 preprint with a similar title is also cited; its date is not established. Floer defines Lagrangian Floer homology under the hypothesis π₂ vanishing for the pair and identifies it with H_*(L₀;ℤ₂) when L₁ is Hamiltonian isotopic to L₀. Secondary sources describe this as the Arnold–Givental count solved in that case. Not opened: described from search snippets of citing pages.
events.delivers: For a Lagrangian pair under the π₂ hypothesis with L₁ Hamiltonian isotopic to L₀ (so L₁ = φ(L₀)), a transverse intersection count at least the total ℤ₂-Betti number of L₀. Restricted to that topological class and to ℤ₂ coefficients as reported by the secondary sources.
events.remains: The Arnold–Givental statement for pairs without the π₂ hypothesis, where bubbling obstructions arise; Lagrangians for which the pair does not satisfy the hypothesis; the strong (Morse critical point) form; the degenerate case.

events.what_happened: Bai and Xu, 'Arnold conjecture over integers', arXiv:2209.08599, v1 only, submitted 18 Sept 2022. Proves that for any closed symplectic manifold the number of 1-periodic orbits of a nondegenerate Hamiltonian is bounded below by a total Betti number over ℤ, accounting for torsion. Built from a Hamiltonian Floer theory over the Novikov ring with integer coefficients and global Kuranishi charts. Opened the abstract page. No journal reference listed. Later secondary sources (Wikipedia, the 2026 Gong preprint) describe the integral case as settled in 2022.

Compiles prior work on the degenerate Arnold conjecture and proposes a proof idea combining the action of quantum cohomology on Floer cohomology with a universal energy estimate for ∂̄_H-holomorphic curves. Claims the degenerate Arnold conjecture in some special cases within Floer theory. events.what_happened: Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu, 'A proof of the Arnold–Givental conjecture', arXiv:2608.27242, v1 only, submitted 27 Aug 2026, math.SG, 69 pages (per aggregator; 158k characters in the HTML). Abstract: for a closed symplectic manifold (X, ω), an anti-symplectic involution τ with fixed locus L, and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ with φ(L) transverse to L, #(φ(L) ∩ L) ≥ dim_F₂ H_*(L;F₂). The method combines integral Floer theory (Bai–Xu), a reduction to Hamiltonian Floer cohomology (Lu), and a localisation in a ℤ/2-equivariant Floer theory. Theorem A in the HTML has the same statement. The authors say the result proves the conjecture 'in full generality' (abstract). Opened the abstract page and the HTML (about 100k of 158k characters read).
events.revisions: Single version, v1 (27 Aug 2026) as of my reading on 11 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: The transverse Arnold–Givental bound over F₂ for Lagrangians that are fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions of closed symplectic manifolds. Restricted to that class and to F₂ coefficients; the authors state F₂ as the right field and treat no other field explicitly.
events.remains: Arnold–Givental for closed Lagrangians that are not fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions (the general statement as the Wikipedia Arnold article gives it); other coefficient fields for real loci; the degenerate form; the strong form.
events.doubts: (a) Scope: the abstract and Theorem A restrict to L = Fix(τ) for an anti-symplectic involution, whereas the general Arnold–Givental statement concerns any closed Lagrangian L. The Wikipedia Arnold conjecture article (rev. 7 Oct 2026) says the authors 'announced a proof of the Arnold–Givental conjecture', which does not mention the restriction. (b) Not refereed: v1 preprint, no journal, no expert commentary or verification found in my searches. (c) The Tracker and Wikipedia are secondary; I did not check whether the preprint's Section 5.2 onward or its references contain further restrictions, since they were not read. (d) Gong's 2026 preprint cites it as 'recently ... proved in full generality [5, Theorem A]': a citing use, not a verification.
events.direction: Proves the transverse Arnold–Givental lower bound over F₂ for real-type Lagrangians (fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions): cuts in favour of the conjecture for that class.

events.what_happened: Gong, 'Two degenerate intersections of Clifford tori in S²×S² and ℂℙ²', arXiv:2610.02965, single version submitted 2 Oct 2026, 23 pages. Abstract: smooth time-periodic Hamiltonians on the monotone manifolds S²×S² and ℂℙ² for which the Clifford torus meets its Hamiltonian image in exactly two isolated degenerate points. The paper says Theorem 1.1 'should be read as a counterexample to the degenerate homological Arnol'd–Givental conjecture', since the transverse bound (1.4) would give 4 = dim H_*(T²;F₂). It also says the 'unrestricted monotone Lagrangian cup-length statement formulated in [15, Conjecture 1] does not hold without an additional hypothesis'. The AI disclosure reads: 'Large language model tools were used to assist in the preparation of this article.' The acknowledgements read: 'My previous work on the degenerate homological Arnol'd-Givental conjecture, combined with AI, led to this paper.' Opened the arXiv abstract page and the HTML (first 100k of 115k characters; the verbatim sentences above were read there).
events.delivers: A counterexample to the degenerate (non-transverse) homological Arnold–Givental bound for the Clifford torus in S²×S² and ℂℙ² (two isolated non-transverse intersection points, with the monotone Hamiltonians the abstract describes). It contradicts the bound of 4 in the degenerate homological form; it is consistent with the bound of 2 for ℂℙⁿ in the author's 2021 paper. It does not test the transverse Arnold–Givental statement, since its intersections are non-transverse.
events.remains: The transverse Arnold–Givental statement (not addressed by this paper); the degenerate statement for other Lagrangians or classes; the Arnold conjecture for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms (not addressed).
events.directly_checkable: The Clifford torus in S²×S² or ℂℙ² and its image under the time-1 map of the stated time-periodic Hamiltonian; the two intersection points and their non-transversality can be checked by hand from the paper's construction (not read in full).
events.doubts: (a) Eight days old at my search; no published response found. (b) The degenerate homological statement that Theorem 1.1 contradicts is the author's own earlier claim (arXiv 2111.15442); the 2026 paper says one conjecture from that earlier paper fails without an extra hypothesis, but the two papers' relationship is not spelled out in full in what I read, so which result the field should believe on the degenerate Clifford tori is not settled by the record. (c) AI: the paper discloses LLM assistance and credits 'combined with AI' with the earlier work leading to the paper; no system is named, and the paper does not say which part of the mathematics the AI produced. (d) Whether the 2022 Hirschi–Porcelli hypotheses exclude these monotone tori was not checked.
events.direction: Cuts against the degenerate homological Lagrangian (Arnold–Givental) bound for the Clifford torus in S²×S² and ℂℙ²; neutral on the transverse statement.
events.object: Smooth time-periodic Hamiltonians on the monotone manifolds S²×S² and ℂℙ² for which the Clifford torus meets its Hamiltonian image in exactly two isolated degenerate (non-transverse) points. The construction is stated as explicit in the abstract ('We construct'); the paper's construction was not read in full.

disputes.summary: Gong's 2021 preprint 2111.15442 (current v5, 12 Sep 2024) claims degenerate homological Lagrangian bounds, including for Clifford tori; Gong's 2 Oct 2026 preprint 2610.02965 says its Theorem 1.1 should be read as a counterexample to the degenerate homological Arnold–Givental conjecture and that a conjecture from 2111.15442 fails without an extra hypothesis. I do not resolve which is right on the degenerate Clifford-torus cases.

The Wikipedia Arnold conjecture article (rev. 7 Oct 2026) says Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu 'announced a proof of the Arnold–Givental conjecture' in August 2026. The arXiv abstract restricts the theorem to Lagrangians that are fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions, while the authors call it 'full generality' for that class. The general Lagrangian case is not claimed in the abstract I read.

Hirschi and Porcelli are reported (Kingy tracker, 26 Aug 2026) to have announced joint work on the same area with no manuscript available; the 2026 Bai et al. preprint's Remark 1.2 mentions the announcement (sentence not read). No manuscript found.

summary: The bullet has three layers, and I searched each. (1) Hamiltonian fixed points, homological form: Floer (monotone, 1988–89), Hofer–Salamon and Ono (semipositive and weakly monotone, 1995), Liu–Tian and Fukaya–Ono (general closed manifolds over ℚ, 1998–99), Pardon (over ℚ, arXiv 2013, G&T 2016), Filippenko–Wehrheim (polyfold, 2018), Abouzaid–Blumberg (fields of characteristic p, arXiv March 2021) and Bai–Xu and Rezchikov (integers, arXiv September 2022) settled the homological form before the window, and no event in the window changes that; the strong (Morse critical point) form and the degenerate cuplength form remain open in general. Within the window, the degenerate Hamiltonian form has partial results: Asselle–Starostka (T^{2m}×ℂℙⁿ, C⁰-close restriction, arXiv Nov 2024, stated open in general), Gong (cuplength estimate on monotone and rational classes, arXiv July 2025) and Jiao (special cases, arXiv June 2026). (2) The transverse Arnold–Givental bound for closed Lagrangians was settled for specific Lagrangians before the window (Givental 1989 and Chang–Jiang 1990 for RP^n in ℂℙⁿ; Oh 1992/1995 for real forms in compact Hermitian symmetric spaces; Frauenfelder 2003 for certain quotient real loci; Lu for weighted projective real loci). The 27 Aug 2026 preprint by Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu claims the full transverse bound over F₂ for real loci (fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions); its abstract restricts to that class, and I found no reading of the abstract that extends it to all closed Lagrangians, though the Wikipedia article's sentence about it does not state the restriction. The paper is a single unrefereed preprint; I found no expert verification, only citations (Gong 2026) and an announced claim from Hirschi and Porcelli with no manuscript. (3) Degenerate Lagrangian intersections: Gong's 2 Oct 2026 preprint gives a counterexample (two isolated non-transverse points for the Clifford torus in S²×S² and ℂℙ²) to the degenerate homological Arnold–Givental bound, and states that the author's own 2021 degenerate claim (arXiv 2111.15442) has a conjecture that fails without an additional hypothesis. AI involvement: none of the classical or Floer-theoretic papers involve AI. The 2026 Bai–Shelukhin–Wang–Xu preprint shows no AI mention in the acknowledgements and in the approximately two-thirds of its text I could read; the tracker's statement that it 'does not disclose a substantive AI role' is a secondary source's paraphrase. The 2026 Gong preprint contains an explicit disclosure ('Large language model tools were used to assist in the preparation of this article') and the acknowledgement 'My previous work ... combined with AI, led to this paper'. No AI system is named there, and the paper does not say what the AI produced, so I have not recorded a named system in ai.systems. Searches for AI credit on any Arnold or Arnold–Givental result (AlphaEvolve, GPT, Gemini, Aristotle, Claude, the OpenAI 722-manuscript release, Lean/Mathlib) found nothing; I did not open the OpenAI CONTENTS.md list, which is the one place a symplectic family could hide.
competing_reading: For the transverse Arnold–Givental statement, the authors' 'full generality' and the Wikipedia wording support reading the 2026 preprint as a full proof of the conjecture as stated in the bullet. The abstract's restriction to fixed loci of anti-symplectic involutions supports reading it as a proof for a real-type subclass only, leaving the general closed Lagrangian case open. For the degenerate Lagrangian case, Gong's 2026 counterexample can be read as refuting the degenerate homological Arnold–Givental statement outright, or as refuting one variant that the bullet does not clearly name, leaving the transverse statement and the degenerate Hamiltonian cuplength form untouched. For AI, the 2026 Gong preprint's disclosure can be read as load-bearing (the author says AI combined with earlier work led to the paper, so AI may have supplied the counterexample idea), or as incidental assistance with preparation, since the paper gives no account of what the AI produced and names no system.
what_would_settle_it: (a) For the transverse statement: an expert reading of arXiv 2608.27242 (in particular whether Theorem A's hypothesis of fixed loci is needed for the argument, and whether Sections 5 onward hold), and a journal decision; and a statement from the authors or a follow-up on whether the method reaches general closed Lagrangians. (b) For the degenerate Lagrangian case: a written response from Gong or others to arXiv 2610.02965, and an explicit comparison with the cuplength hypothesis in 2111.15442 Conjecture 1 and with Hirschi–Porcelli 2211.07559 (whether its orientation and relative-exactness hypotheses exclude the monotone Clifford tori). (c) For AI: the full text of 2610.02965 with the sentence that identifies the system (if any) and the part of the argument it produced; the Hirschi–Porcelli manuscript, if it appears; and the openai/math CONTENTS.md list, checked for symplectic families.
